title: Expand self-signification model beyond triads
description:
Expand self-signification model beyond triads. Significant design decision — direction not yet decided on product side, but extensibility point must be introduced in feedback-mct.

MINIMUM VIABLE EXTENSIBILITY (Codex — introduce in feedback-mct):
  class TriadResponse(BaseModel): kind: Literal['triad'], signifier_id: str, x: float, y: float
  class DyadResponse(BaseModel): kind: Literal['dyad'], signifier_id: str, value: float
  class ChoiceResponse(BaseModel): kind: Literal['choice'], signifier_id: str, selected: list[str]
  SignifierResponse = Annotated[TriadResponse | DyadResponse | ChoiceResponse, Field(discriminator='kind')]

No new top-level story fields per signifier type — all responses go in StorySignification.responses.

BLOCKED ON PRODUCT DECISION: what signifier types to actually support and what they should express for this domain. Hardcoded 3-triad constraint is removed in feedback-mct which unblocks the technical extensibility. Actual dyad/choice product work is deferred until product direction is clear.

USER NOTE: current triads are placeholders. Signifier design (what tensions/qualities to make visible) is a product/deployment decision separate from the backend — labels come from config, not code. Backend works the same regardless of axis meaning.

title: Align theme types: adapters return dicts but storage/domain expect strings

EntityExtraction.themes was widened to List[Any] as a temporary fix in feedback-vk7. Proper fix: decide on one representation (likely extract theme name strings in the service or adapters) and tighten the type back to List[str] throughout.

title: Improve insight trust model: distinguish evidence from interpretation

Currently narrative synthesis is presented alongside story counts but without clear separation of what is retrieved evidence vs LLM-generated interpretation. Needed: prominently show sample sizes and confidence framing, make it easy to inspect the supporting stories behind any synthesized insight, add caveats systematically rather than optionally, visually distinguish participant-provided content from machine-generated content. Relates to feedback-gcl (product decision on LLM role).

description: Current analysis surfaces pattern counts and clusters. Missing: weak-signal detection (patterns that appear rarely but may be significant), confidence indicators on insights (how many stories, how consistent), cross-segment comparison (e.g. how does theme distribution differ between departments), richer temporal interpretation beyond window counts, stronger use of entity relationships from graph. DIRECTION NEEDED: prioritise which of these to implement first and in what form — they are independent capabilities but share some infrastructure.

description: Entity extraction and sentiment extraction each independently write processing_status to 'processed' or 'failed'. Last writer wins regardless of the other stage's outcome. Direction unclear — needs design decision before implementation: option A is separate stage fields on the Story document, option B is a pipeline orchestrator service that is the only writer of processing_status.

title: Story 3.2: Create Entity Nodes and Relationships
BUG: MongoDB and Neo4j story datasets appear out of sync
description:
Live data review found a major mismatch between raw storage and graph projection: MongoDB feedback.stories contained 16 stories, while Neo4j contained 70 Story nodes. This suggests stale graph data, missing cleanup, or lack of reconciliation/reprojection. Impact: graph-based exploration may operate over a different dataset than the raw story corpus, undermining trust in patterns and drill-down. Needed: determine source of drift, add reconciliation/rebuild support, and ensure graph projection reflects the current Mongo corpus.

--- Claude notes (2026-03-22) ---

The 70 Neo4j nodes vs 16 MongoDB stories gap is almost certainly explained by reprocessing history. The /reprocess endpoint (feedback-cv7) was used multiple times during live testing, and _save_story_to_graph() does a MERGE not a replace - each reprocess pass creates additional nodes if story_id matching isn't exact, or creates duplicate entity/theme nodes. Additionally, stories that were submitted and then deleted from Mongo would leave orphan nodes in Neo4j since there is no deletion propagation.

The practical risk: /api/patterns/by-entity/{name} and theme/correlation queries all run against Neo4j. If 54 of those 70 nodes are stale/orphaned, pattern counts are inflated and potentially misleading.

Immediate diagnostic step: run a Cypher query counting Story nodes and check how many have matching MongoDB _ids. That will tell us whether this is duplicates or orphans.

Longer-term fix options:
1. Add ON CONFLICT/MERGE semantics in save_story_node so reprocessing is idempotent (minimal change)
2. Add a reconciliation script that deletes Neo4j nodes with no corresponding MongoDB story (safer)
3. Both - idempotent writes AND a one-time cleanup

BUG: UI story submission does not trigger LLM processing
description:
Stories submitted through the main UI (/submit HTMX path in src/api/ui.py) call service.submit_story() directly without wiring BackgroundTasks. Entity extraction, sentiment extraction, and graph projection are never triggered. Stories submitted via the UI remain permanently in 'pending' state unless manually reprocessed via the /reprocess endpoint.

Stories submitted via the JSON API (POST /api/stories) are unaffected — that path correctly wires background_tasks.

FIX: Add BackgroundTasks dependency to the UI submit handler and call _process_story() as a background task, matching the pattern in src/api/stories.py submit_story().

title: Improve theme extraction so themes aggregate as stable labels
description:
Live data review found extracted themes are often too verbose and too unique to aggregate well, e.g. 'The importance of collaboration and community knowledge' or 'Learning through explanation over mere fixing'. They behave more like mini-summaries than canonical theme labels. Needed: normalize theme extraction toward shorter stable labels, or split theme output into a canonical label plus optional richer explanation.

--- Claude notes (2026-03-22) ---

Confirmed via live API inspection: 10 processed stories produced 25 distinct themes with every theme at count=1. Zero aggregation is happening. The synthesis endpoint generates themes on-the-fly per call and produced 31 more, none matching the stored ones.

There are three distinct problems here, not one:

1. Theme verbosity: labels are narrative sentences, not stable tokens. 'Loss of Skill' and 'Dependence on Technology' refer to the same story concept but appear as separate themes.

2. No normalisation between stored themes (written during extract_for_story) and synthesis-time themes (generated fresh per synthesis call). These two theme sets never meet.

3. No cross-story deduplication: 'Efficiency Enhancement' and 'Efficiency Over Implementation' and 'Efficiency and Productivity' are all count=1 when they likely describe the same cluster.

Possible approaches (in order of implementation cost):

A. Prompt engineering: instruct llama3 to choose from a fixed candidate list of ~15-20 themes, falling back to a short label form only if no candidate fits. Cheapest, but fragile against model drift.

B. Post-extraction normalisation: embed extracted themes and cluster at query time, grouping near-duplicates before returning counts. More robust but needs embeddings infrastructure.

C. Separate extraction from labelling: store raw theme text, then run a separate normalisation pass that maps raw → canonical using LLM or fuzzy match. Decouples extraction quality from aggregation quality.

Option A is the right MVP fix. Option C is the right longer-term architecture. Option B requires embedding infrastructure not currently in scope.

Also relevant: entity extraction shows the same fragmentation problem. 'AI', 'AI assistants', 'Claude' are all separate entities when they represent the same analytical concept. A controlled vocabulary or entity normalisation pass would help both.

title: Add participant-authored headline field to story capture
description:
Add participant-authored headline field to story capture. Absorbed into feedback-mct — headline lands inside StorySignification, not as a top-level Story field.

Implementation is part of feedback-mct scope:
- StorySignification.headline: str | None = None
- StorySubmissionRequest includes optional headline
- MongoDB storage reads/writes signification.headline
- API response exposes headline
- Submission UI adds optional field with prompt: 'How would you describe this experience in one sentence?' (not 'title' — invites interpretation not filing)

EXECUTION: close this ticket when feedback-mct is merged; no separate implementation needed.

title: Story 4.1: Query Stories by Entity
Prepare architecture for triad pool and randomisation
description: Currently triads are a fixed set loaded from config/triads.yaml at startup, and all stories are required to have placements for every triad. This makes pattern analysis clean but reduces SenseMaker fidelity (Snowden's original design uses a pool of signifiers with randomised subsets shown to participants, reducing researcher framing bias and participant fatigue). Investigate what would need to change to support: (1) a larger pool of triads in config, (2) participants seeing a randomised subset per submission, (3) pattern analysis that handles sparse triad coverage across stories (not every story has every triad). Key constraint: proximity clustering and correlation analysis currently assume consistent dimensionality. This is low priority until the dataset is large enough (hundreds of stories, multiple teams) for per-triad patterns to be statistically meaningful. At small scale, fixed triads are the right call.

title: Story 2.4: Analyze Sentiment and Emotional Tone
Story 5.1: Background processing worker with Redis queue
description: Decouple LLM processing from the HTTP request lifecycle. Currently EntityExtractionService and SentimentService run as FastAPI BackgroundTasks in the same process — LLM timeouts block worker threads. Solution: separate worker process that BLPOPs from a Redis queue (populated at submission) for low-latency pickup, plus a periodic sweep of MongoDB for pending/failed stories as a fallback. Worker retries failed stories with backoff. Submission endpoint pushes story_id to Redis and returns immediately. Removes BackgroundTasks from the API layer entirely. Also remove the temporary POST /api/stories/{id}/reprocess endpoint added as a stopgap (feedback-cv7 dependency) — it exists only to process stories submitted before the worker is in place.

Users are not told this constraint, so reasonable questions like topic+sentiment queries fail in confusing ways. title: Story 3.3: Create Theme Nodes and Clustering

Product decision: LLM as facilitator vs interpreter of record
description: The current design has an unresolved epistemic tension. Original SenseMaker: participants signify their own experience, analysts inspect aggregate distributions, machine-generated narrative stays downstream of that. Current risk: the LLM synthesis feature risks becoming 'LLM explains the dataset' rather than 'system surfaces patterns, humans interpret them.' DECISION NEEDED before further insight UI work: (1) What role should LLM synthesis play — drafting hypotheses for human review, or providing conclusions? (2) Should the UI clearly distinguish participant-provided narrative, participant triad placements, graph-derived structural patterns, and LLM-generated synthesis as separate epistemic layers? (3) Should LLM output be framed explicitly as provisional interpretation? This is a product/methodology decision, not a code decision. Outcome should produce concrete constraints for feedback-zfs (spatial drill-down) and any future insight UI work.

Separate contextual metadata from interpretive metadata in domain model
description:
Separate contextual metadata from interpretive/signification metadata in the domain model. Current StoryMetadata mixes administrative fields with no epistemic separation.

THREE-WAY SPLIT (from Codex review):
- context_metadata: department, role, tool_context (segmentation data)
- participant_metadata: user_pseudonym (identity, neither context nor signification)
- signification: triads + headline (feedback-bkf) + future signifier responses (feedback-0ct)

This ticket absorbs the structural parts of feedback-bkf (headline lands in signification, not top-level) and introduces the SignifierResponse discriminated union needed by feedback-0ct.

DOMAIN MODEL:
  class ContextMetadata(BaseModel): department, role, tool_context
  class ParticipantMetadata(BaseModel): user_pseudonym
  class SignifierResponse (discriminated union): TriadResponse | DyadResponse | ChoiceResponse
  class StorySignification(BaseModel): headline, responses: list[SignifierResponse]
  Story: context_metadata, participant_metadata, signification

CONSTRAINTS:
- Remove min_length=3, max_length=3 on triads in Story and StorySubmissionRequest (blocker for feedback-0ct)
- Replace with: at least one signification response required at submission

BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY:
- MongoDB adapter reads both V1 (flat metadata.*) and V2 shapes
- Add schema_version field to new documents
- Write only V2 once deployed
- Neo4j: no migration needed — coordinates were never stored there (Story 3.4 deferred, never implemented)
- Deprecated story.triads accessor for one transition period

ALSO FIXES: relax the hardcoded 3-triad constraint that blocks feedback-0ct

title: Make metadata a first-class analysis surface for filtering and comparison
description:
Metadata as first-class analysis surface. Scoped to signification-layer analysis — how do triad distributions differ by role/department? Not just BI filtering of themes.

DEPENDS ON: feedback-mct (clean context_metadata / signification split)

SCOPE:
- Consistent context_metadata filtering across themes, entities, correlations, clustering endpoints (department/role slicing for segmentation)
- Signification-layer comparison: triad distribution differences across subgroups
- Questions like 'do people who place toward constraint-novel use different language?' or 'does triad distribution differ between junior/senior roles?'

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: making the LLM theme/entity counts more filterable as the primary surface. Segmentation is context, not the analytical primary.

Temporal filtering is already in-memory in pattern_query.py — decision needed on whether to push filtering to graph layer or keep in-memory at this scale.

title: BUG: reprocess endpoint catches KeyError instead of NotFoundError
description: POST /api/stories/{id}/reprocess catches KeyError to detect missing stories, but StoragePort.get_story() raises NotFoundError. A missing story can surface as a 500 instead of a 404. Quick fix: catch NotFoundError from src.ports.errors.

Especially problematic for LLM-backed operations (30-60s response times). Needs: visible loading indicators on form submit, disabled state or acknowledgement while in-flight, clear success/error distinction. hx-indicator is already used on the dashboard entity buttons but not consistently elsewhere.

title: BUG: Sentiment extraction outputs are not schema-constrained enough for aggregation
description:
Live data review found process_sentiment/outcome_sentiment values such as 'neutral (acknowledging a change in approach)', 'positive (embracing the new process as more effective)', 'neutral with a hint of negativity', and 'cautious'. Downstream aggregation code expects exact categorical values like positive/negative/neutral, so these free-form variants do not count correctly. Fix by constraining sentiment extraction to a strict enum for the categorical fields and, if needed, storing richer explanation in separate fields.

--- Claude notes (2026-03-22) ---

Confirmed via live synthesis call: theme_counts in the synthesis response contained 31 distinct themes across 7 stories, many with free-form values. The sentiment_summary showed only 1 positive_process and 1 negative_process for 7 stories, which suggests 5 stories' process_sentiment values didn't match the aggregation enum at all.

The fix has two layers:

1. LLM prompt: the Ollama/llama3 prompt for sentiment extraction must explicitly instruct the model to return ONLY the words 'positive', 'negative', or 'neutral' for the categorical fields - no parenthetical explanations. The current prompt presumably doesn't enforce this.

2. Validation/normalisation on ingest: SentimentExtractionService (or the LLM adapter) should validate and normalise the returned values before storing. A simple approach: if the value starts with 'positive' use 'positive', etc. This handles model drift without needing a prompt change alone.

3. Domain model: SentimentAnalysis.process_sentiment and outcome_sentiment could be typed as Literal['positive', 'negative', 'neutral'] to make the constraint explicit and catch violations at parse time.

The emotion_markers list is less critical since it is stored as free-form and not aggregated.

title: BUG: Race condition between graph save and entity extraction
description: submit_story() schedules _save_story_to_graph(), entity_service.extract_for_story(), and sentiment_service.extract_for_story() as independent background tasks. EntityExtractionService can call graph_projection.project_story() before _save_story_to_graph() has created the Story node in Neo4j. Entity/Theme nodes get created but no relationships to the Story node exist. No retry or reconciliation step. Fix requires deterministic ordering: graph save must complete before extraction tasks begin, or extraction must not trigger graph projection until the story node is confirmed present. Relates to feedback-cv7 (background worker) — the proper fix is likely to sequence these inside the worker, not in FastAPI background tasks.

title: Workflow: consolidate AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md into one canonical instruction file
description: The repo currently maintains both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md with overlapping workflow and architecture guidance. This creates a drift risk over time: different agents may privilege different files, instructions can diverge subtly, and repo policy ends up split across two sources of truth. Proposed direction: choose one canonical file for repo instructions, and make the other a symlink or thin compatibility pointer to it. Also review whether the instruction set has become too large/noisy and trim or restructure if necessary, but the primary issue is duplicated authority rather than size alone.

title: Spatial drill-down as first-class interaction
description:
Spatial drill-down as first-class interaction. Visual display of story distributions in each triad triangle, click/brush region → see stories there with headlines. Themes/entities as secondary overlays.

DEPENDS ON: feedback-mct (for clean signification model and headline)

KEY ARCHITECTURAL FINDING (Codex):
Triad coordinates are NOT stored in Neo4j — Story 3.4 deferred this and it was never implemented. Neo4jGraphAdapter.save_story_node() accepts triads but silently ignores coordinates. Spatial queries MUST come from MongoDB (StoragePort), not GraphPort. This aligns with evidence-first philosophy — participant evidence stays in raw storage.

API SHAPE:
  POST /api/signifiers/{signifier_id}/stories/query
  { 'selection': { 'kind': 'polygon', 'points': [{x, y}, ...] }, 'limit': 50, 'offset': 0, 'include_overlays': true }
  Response: id, headline, story_excerpt, coordinates, timestamp, context_metadata, optional themes/entities

Polygon (not bounding box) supports click-bucket, brush, and lasso UIs without API redesign.

StoragePort gets find_stories_in_polygon(signifier_id, polygon_points) method.

INTERACTION MODEL (non-negotiable):
1. Dashboard leads with triad scatter/density per signifier
2. Select region → immediately see stories (with headlines)
3. Optional: 'what patterns do these stories share?' → theme/entity overlay or synthesis
4. LLM synthesis never shown first

ALSO NOTE: add coordinate validation server-side (point inside triangle, not just 0≤x,y≤1).
